speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has been more than a month since the 1 February 2021 detention of Myanmar's civilian government leaders including President U Win Myint and State Counsellor Daw Aung San Suu Kyi.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The situation in Myanmar unfortunately remains fraught with much uncertainty and there remains significant risk of escalation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: MFA has strongly advised all Singaporeans to defer travel to Myanmar at this time and we have also advised Singaporeans who are currently in Myanmar to consider leaving as soon as they can by commercial means whilst flights are still available.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have spoken extensively on Singapore's response to these developments in Myanmar, including during my Ministry's Committee of Supply (COS) debate on 1 March.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On 2 March, I joined other ASEAN Foreign Ministers via video-conference for an Informal ASEAN Ministerial Meeting (IAMM).

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At that meeting, the representative of Myanmar's military authorities, Mr Wunna Maung Lwin also briefed us on his account.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore believes that ASEAN should play a constructive role in facilitating a return to normalcy and hopefully, stability in Myanmar, in line with the principles enshrined in the ASEAN Charter.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Chair of ASEAN issued a Statement on 1 February, the very day the NLD government was ousted.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Informal ASEAN Ministerial Meeting (IAMM) I referred to earlier, was convened on 2 March 2021.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The meeting reaffirmed the practice for ASEAN to discuss important issues of common concern whenever they arise.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This meeting was an opportunity to have frank and open, candid discussions, and to reflect the international community's concerns directly to the representative of the military authorities.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Members would be aware of the media coverage of that meeting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also provided a full transcript of my intervention during that meeting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I conveyed Singapore's grave concerns over the situation in Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are appalled by violence, inflicted by security forces against civilians.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is the height of national shame for the armed forces of any country to turn its arms against its own people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The use of lethal force against unarmed civilians is inexcusable under any circumstances.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The immediate concern is to step back from a rapidly deteriorating situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I called on the military authorities to seek a peaceful solution for Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The alternative is prolonged instability and to quote Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, "an enormous tragic step back" for Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The military is an institution in the body politic of Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, the military authorities in Myanmar played a role in Myanmar’s political journey towards democracy in the past decade.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has to reach a modus vivendi with the other key stakeholders in Myanmar including Daw Aung San Suu Kyi.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There remain prospects for a peaceful resolution as long as all sides can come together, engage in genuine and direct dialogue, and find a way to return to Myanmar’s democratic transition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We thus hope that the military authorities will release President Win Myint and State Counsellor Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, so that these discussions can commence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also support a visit by the Special Envoy of the United Nation Secretary General to Myanmar, Ms Christine Burgener, and hope that she will also be given access during her visit to Daw Aung San Suu Kyi and other NLD leaders.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If tensions do not abate, the longer term stability of our region will also be affected, with potential serious consequences for everyone.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There will also be further humanitarian impact given the current severe COVID-19 and economic stresses confronting their people, and do not forget the unresolved resettlement of displaced persons from Rakhine State.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore's assistance to the displaced persons from Rakhine State is on-going.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also made contributions through the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Reflecting the generosity of Singaporeans, our private sector and community organisations have also stepped up, raising funds to provide for the material needs of those in the refugee camps.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Unfortunately, the COVID-19 pandemic last year also compromised the delivery of some of this humanitarian assistance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is important to resume efforts to ensure the safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation of refugees back to Rakhine State.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have lent strong support towards ASEAN's efforts to help improve the ground conditions in Rakhine State, such as through the Preliminary Needs Assessment (PNA) and the ASEAN Secretariat's Ad-Hoc Support Teams, which focused on implementing the recommendations of the PNA teams.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These recommendations include priority projects, such as the supply of radio receivers to the local community, in order to strengthen the dissemination of accurate information.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are prepared to send further consignments of aid and stand ready to support future comprehensive needs assessments once repatriation commences, so that we can be more targeted in helping the displaced persons.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But at the end of the day, the solution to both the political and the humanitarian problems lie within Myanmar itself and in the hands of its people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We hope to see an outcome that reflects the interests and the will of the people of Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think since I filed this question several days ago, the situation seems to to have worsened.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I just have one supplementary question for the Foreign Minister, which is that at the ASEAN level, is this being monitored with a view to keeping other options open to nudge the government in Myanmar towards reconciliation, towards political settlement, should the situation worsen even further in the days and weeks ahead?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have raised this issue in Parliament quite a number of times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know the Minister is deeply concerned about the refugees as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Like him, I have been to the refugee camps in Cox's Bazaar and it really is suffering at a scale that is unimaginable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met many of the children there, many of whom have watched both fathers and mothers get killed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I really hope and I asked MFA to consider sending another consignment of humanitarian aid this year, and that will really help the refugees that are currently in Cox's Bazaar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, the more fundamental political and violent events occurring within Myanmar itself complicate any attempts to address this humanitarian disaster, but we will continue to look out for opportunities.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My supplementary question refers to two instruments: the ASEAN Charter and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the discussions with Minister's counterparts in ASEAN, would reference be made to both those instruments and the general principles elucidated in those instruments, to have some level of forbearance over the actions of the military in Myanmar?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My view is that the actions do go against the whole tenor and principles laid down in the ASEAN Charter and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I also want the House to have a realistic assessment of the factors at play.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The history of Myanmar over the past 70 years, and I mentioned that earlier this week, is a long and tortured history of a large, wealthy talented country, unable to come together and achieve national unity, unable to reconcile differences between ethnic groups, political ideologies, between the different pillars of the political construct that is Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we do need to be realistic in what we say or do.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I want to emphasise that my key objective – again, perhaps, influenced by my medical background – is, first, do no harm.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is a limit to how far external pressure will be brought to bear.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It does not mean we approve of what they have done and how they do it, and we are clear in our expressions of disapproval.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But let us also be realistic and let us hope that good sense prevails.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are also profound lessons for us in Singapore, to count our blessings since Independence, that we have been able to come together as one people, regardless of race, language or religion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have been able to build a democracy that functions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We really have so much to be thankful for and to count our blessings in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Question Nos 5 and 8 have been postponed to the sitting of Parliament on 8 March 2021.]
